_readme: THE BOX ROLL-CALL. Every mechanism that is supposed to be running on meepo-ec2,
with the heartbeat that would prove it, the allowance past which that heartbeat is
old, and THE NAME OF WHOEVER DECIDED IT RUNS. Read by tools/box-rollcall.mjs; run
on the box by deploy/box-rollcall.sh; wired into Wright's daily operator round.
WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-27 the town was carrying four mechanisms that had been
BUILT and were not RUNNING, and no surface anywhere went red about any of them:
the world drain had no caller at all (postmark#1990), the settlement shadow was
disabled with a WOULD-REFUSE verdict nobody had read (2 days 8 hours old), the
economy report's timer had been owed since 2026-08-10 in OPERATIONS.md's own Known
gaps, and the stripe watcher was built on 08-25 and never adopted. Three of those
are failures; the fourth is correct and deliberate. A roll-call that could not tell
them apart would be no better than the silence it replaces, which is why PARKED is
a first-class verdict here and a parked row is carried FOREVER rather than omitted.
THE LAW THIS SERVES (OPERATIONS.md § Built is not Done): a mechanism folds only
with its runner, its liveness check, and its activation owner named.
ADDING A ROW. Every postmark-* timer on the box, and every ENABLED postmark-*
service, must appear here — the checker globs the box and reports ALARM-unmanifested
for anything it finds that this file does not name, which is what keeps the roll-call
from decaying into a snapshot of the day it was written. Parked rows are legal.
Omission is not.
FIELDS.
unit                  the systemd unit, exactly as systemctl names it
label                 how the alarm line refers to it, in the town's own words
stage                 live | parked. parked never alarms for being inert — but it
DOES alarm if the box has it enabled, because then the
manifest and the box disagree about whether it is inert
activation_owner      who decided it runs, and the receipt. Not decoration: a row
that cannot say this is a row nobody will fix when it reddens
cadence               the effective schedule, in prose
cadence_source        WHERE that schedule is authoritative. Note that this is
`systemctl show -p TimersCalendar` for every timer and never
the .timer file — postmark-dev-freshen's file says every ten
minutes and its drop-in makes it daily, a factor of 144
heartbeat             what would prove it ran. unit_trigger = systemd's own last
firing; state_file = the work's own output (stronger — it
proves the run REACHED ITS END); unit_active = a daemon, whose
liveness is simply that it is up
stale_means           the sentence the operator reads at 8am: what it means for THIS
unit to be late, and why the allowance is that number
no_staleness_because  the only escape from an allowance, and deliberately a sentence
outcome               judges what the rail PRODUCED, not just that it ran — a rolling
Inside it: history_path · alarm_on_classes (terminal on sight) ·
zero_published_runs (the starvation window) · means (the ONE sentence
the board prints) · why (the paragraph a reviewer weighs, never printed
— a board that recites its own rationale every morning teaches skimming)
receipt log, the refusal classes that are terminal on sight, and
how many consecutive empty runs is starvation. Every threshold is
DATA here rather than a constant in the checker, because a baseline
compiled into code is a number nobody can review beside its reason
SEE ALSO the custody[] block at the foot of this file: every row above asks whether a
mechanism RAN; those ask whether it still CAN.

units.label: the ferry
units.activation_owner: Keemin — the town's published crossings; consolidated onto the box 2026-07-08 (deploy/DEPLOY.md § The ferry on the box), unit added to the repo 2026-08-01 c8e62f9
units.stale_means: A missed crossing means mail written yesterday did not deliver and the ledger carries no stamp for it. The allowance is one crossing plus an hour: a single late tick is Persistent=true catching up after a reboot, but two crossings of silence is the town's clock stopped.

units.label: the crossing save
units.activation_owner: Wright — added 2026-08-09 45b9dcf, crossing-aligned two minutes behind the ferry so the two never contend for town.lock
units.cadence: 00:02 and 12:02 UTC, two minutes behind each crossing on purpose
units.stale_means: The dynamic store is not crystallized at the boundary it just left, so the record of that crossing has a hole in it that no later run fills — the save writes the crossing it has left, not the ones it slept through. Same allowance as the ferry it follows.

units.label: the office's read index
units.activation_owner: Keemin — part of the original box standup, enabled in DEPLOY.md § One-time setup's own enable line; unit added 2026-08-01 c8e62f9
units.cadence: every 15 minutes at :07, :22, :37, :52 — offset from the site extractor
units.stale_means: The office serves a frozen X-Postmark-As-Of: every door answers 200 with yesterday's town. This is the exact failure found BY HAND on 2026-08-25 (one distinct as-of across 40 minutes and three tick slots). The allowance is three ticks — one missed tick is noise, three is a stuck rehydrate. site-sentinel's office_as_of probe watches the OUTCOME of this from outside; this row watches the runner.

units.label: the harbor watch
units.activation_owner: Wright — added 2026-08-16 71a4622 for the web-of-towns carriage duty; read every operator round at step 4.7
units.stale_means: Cargo left at a foreign pier goes unseen, and the operator round reads a snapshot that describes the shores as they were rather than as they are — the sable-#537 shape, where carriage was owed and nobody could see it. The allowance is three ticks plus the jitter. The stamp is read from inside the file rather than from its mtime because a snapshot rewritten with unchanged content still has a fresh mtime.

units.label: the usdc watch
units.activation_owner: Wright — the funding lane, unit added 2026-08-24 00e3d64; adopted as a READ-ONLY watcher (it sees and reports; it does not witness)
units.stale_means: Arrivals at the town's intake address stop being noticed, and because the cursor only advances on a successful read, a long silence means real money has landed with nobody told. The allowance is three ticks. Note that this row and site-sentinel's usdc_watch probe are deliberate duplicates: the sentinel reads it from the town's outside, this reads the runner from the box's inside, and the pair survives either one being the thing that broke.

units.label: the site sentinel
units.activation_owner: Wright — built and enabled 2026-08-25 b71f63a, on Keemin's sentence "how can we LOUDLY BE NOTIFIED when something is down on the site?"; enable line in DEPLOY.md § The site sentinel
units.stale_means: THE WATCHMAN ITSELF HAS STOPPED, and it is the one failure the sentinel is structurally incapable of reporting — its own header says so: 'it cannot see its own death'. A dead sentinel presents as a permanently green board, which is worse than no board. This row is the answer to that, and it is the single most load-bearing row in this file. The allowance is three ticks.

units.label: the settlement sweep
units.activation_owner: Wright — added 2026-08-17 2cc4c6b, timed 05:45/17:45 UTC to land ahead of the Worldkeeper's 06:00/18:00 heartbeats so his blessing certifies fresh work
units.stale_means: Drafts stop settling into the world: residents' work sits eligible and unpublished, and the world pin stops advancing twice daily as the law requires. The allowance is one crossing plus an hour. The stamp is the verdict's own 'at' rather than the file's mtime, because a run that refuses still rewrites the file — the question is when it last DECIDED, not when the bytes last moved.

outcome.why: THE CLOCK IS NOT THE WORK. Until 2026-08-30 this row judged timer recency and nothing else, so the board would have read a green tick over the night of 08-31: the timer fired at 02:38:50Z exactly as scheduled and the crossing refused at 02:39:26Z with {"phase":"unknown"}, publishing nothing. TWO SHAPES ARE JUDGED HERE AND THEY FAIL DIFFERENTLY. A canon-bad refusal (deploy/settlement-classify.mjs) is loud and instantaneous — the failing path is in origin/main s own tree, so no rerun ever clears it and one occurrence is already forever; it alarms on sight. STARVATION is quiet and only exists across crossings: on 2026-08-26 a crossing left 42 marks drafted and reported nothing, and a starving crossing printed 0 published, 0 unpublished and read as a quiet day for two days — every receipt individually honest, the pattern the finding. Three consecutive crossings that published nothing WHILE left_drafted grew is work arriving with none getting out. THE WINDOW IS THREE because two is a weekend of genuinely nothing eligible and four is two full days of silence, which is the length the 08-26 starvation actually ran. The log is written by deploy/settlement-history.mjs at the end of every decided crossing; a single receipt file is overwritten twice a day and structurally cannot hold a pattern. AND A REFUSAL THAT KEEPS COMING BACK: the class rule above catches the refusal that announces itself terminal; unsettled_runs catches the one that does not and is terminal anyway. postmark-world 7f866059 (2026-08-30 22:40) says it in its own message — the fault "was the sweep s standing 2-error lint refusal (every crossing since 08-28 re-drained them, dropped one, tripped on the other)": six input-bad refusals over three days, each individually rerunnable, none ever cleared, because what produced them was upstream of the rerun. It is judged on STATUS and not on left_drafted, because a refused crossing never reaches the point of having channel counts — its receipt carries zeros, so the starvation rule is structurally blind to it.
outcome.means: Read the receipt at /srv/postmark-harbor/settlement-auto.json — its `class` and `next_step` say whether this is yours to rerun or yours to repair. INSTALL-DAY NOTE: this row is EXPECTED to read ALARM-outcome until the first crossing after deploy writes the log, and it clears itself then.

units.label: the settlement shadow
units.activation_owner: Wright — built 2026-08-20 1f3a73a, and DELIBERATELY REACTIVATED 2026-08-23 998c5d1 after the outage-day disable, at a reduced 2/day cadence chosen so the CPU cost stopped being an argument for switching it off. The commit message is the receipt: 'reactivated 2026-08-23 after the outage-day disable'.
units.cadence: 10:23 and 22:23 UTC — off the real crossing's 05:45/17:45 marks so the rehearsal never races the pen
units.stale_means: THIS IS THE ROW THE ROLL-CALL WAS BUILT AROUND, and on install day it is expected to be red. The shadow rehearses the next crossing with the pen denied, so a WOULD-REFUSE here is a finding roughly twelve hours ahead of the real settlement rather than an outage. On 2026-08-27 the box had this timer disabled, and the verdict on disk read {"at":"2026-08-24T22:23:00Z","status":"would-refuse","detail":"grammar suite would go red"} — the exact finding it exists to raise, 2 days 8 hours old when measured at 2026-08-27T06:00Z, unread. The repo says reactivated and the box says disabled, and until this file existed nothing anywhere could see the two disagree. Its own script header claims the verdict is 'polled by the ops page and read on the operator round'; no step of the operator round read it. The allowance is one cadence period plus an hour.

units.label: the dev sandbox freshen
units.activation_owner: Keemin — founder ruling 2026-08-26 (the drop-in carries it verbatim: 'dev default = sandbox/seed; nightly stand-back, not 10-minute — a mid-day rehearsal is never yanked'); unit added 2026-08-21 27026cd
units.cadence_source: systemctl show postmark-dev-freshen.timer -p TimersCalendar — AND NOTHING ELSE. The .timer file itself says OnCalendar=*:0/10 and calls itself 'every 10 minutes' in its own Description; the drop-in at postmark-dev-freshen.timer.d/nightly.conf clears that line and substitutes the daily one. Reading the file instead of the merged value is wrong by a factor of 144 in the direction of alarming on a healthy rail every ten minutes forever.
units.stale_means: dev stops returning to the certified sandbox/seed snapshot, so a rehearsal run against dev is measuring drift rather than the seed. The allowance is 26 hours — one full day plus room for the box to have been down over the 08:10 mark and caught up on boot.

units.label: the office API
units.activation_owner: Keemin — the front door itself; enabled in DEPLOY.md § One-time setup's enable line, unit added 2026-08-01 c8e62f9
units.no_staleness_because: A daemon has no cadence to be late for — its liveness is simply that it is up, which is the check the row above the heartbeat already makes. What the uptime is reported FOR is the flap: an office that came up four minutes ago every single morning is a crash loop wearing a green tick, and only the number makes that visible.
units.stale_means: Not applicable. Down is the failure, and down is caught as ALARM-disabled. site-sentinel's office_api probe watches the same thing from outside the box; both are kept, because a door that answers 200 to the outside while systemd reports it restarting is a finding, and so is the reverse.

units.label: the dev office
units.activation_owner: Wright — the dev sandbox standup, unit installed 2026-08-22; behind Cloudflare Access by design
units.no_staleness_because: Same as the office it mirrors: an always-on daemon is judged by being up, not by being recent. Its uptime is carried for the same flap reason.
units.stale_means: Not applicable. Down means dev.postmark.town stops answering behind the Access gate, which reads to the sentinel as an INFO 302 either way — so this row is the only place a dead dev office is visible.

units.label: the stripe watch (Stage B)
units.activation_owner: Keemin — ADOPTED 2026-08-27 ~00:15 EDT (the founder's ON word, the night of the martina $20; enabled by Wright 06:23Z after review of wright/stripe-login-attribution). The Stage-B header's condition was met: the paste became the outage.
units.cadence: every 15 minutes at :07/:22/:37/:52 — offset from usdc-watch so the two funding watchers never contend for town.lock
units.cadence_source: systemctl show postmark-stripe-watch.timer -p TimersCalendar — measured on the box 2026-08-31T03:4xZ: '{ OnCalendar=*-*-* *:07/15:00 }', UnitFileState=enabled, ActiveState=active
units.stale_means: Stripe payments stop being attributed: a resident pays and the funding ledger does not learn, so the town's own record of who is paid up goes quietly wrong rather than loudly absent. The allowance is three ticks. WHAT THIS ROW HAS ALREADY CAUGHT ONCE, and the reason it judges the unit before the heartbeat: on 2026-08-27 a file at /srv/postmark-office/.stripe-watch-state.json was four minutes fresh, written by a HAND-RUN of the tool's default state path, while no unit existed on the box at all. That file is not this row's heartbeat and must never become it — a hand-run's output is exactly the evidence that makes a rail with no runner look alive. THE ROW'S OWN SCAR (2026-08-30, the v1 sweep): this rail was adopted on 08-27 by flipping stage parked -> live, and every sentence around that word stayed written for a rail that does not run — cadence said 'would be … once adopted', cadence_source said 'the unit is not on the box', and parked_because and adopt_command were both still standing. The suite went red for three weeks about a manifest that described the wrong box, which is this file's own failure class committed inside this file.

units.label: the box publishes the site (atomic swap, lock, convergence)
units.activation_owner: Keemin — AC #3 of the 2026-08-27 acceptance criteria; installed+enabled by Wright 06:33Z after selftest 33/33 and a proven sandbox first run (3347 pages). GitHub schedule retires only after one proven box crossing.
units.cadence: every 30 minutes at :10/:40 — phased ~10 min after the ferry crossings
units.stale_means: The site stops following the town: a ferry landing never reaches postmark.town, and nothing else publishes prod now that the box is the one writer. The allowance is three ticks plus build time.

units.label: the World 2.0 candle
units.activation_owner: Wright — founder ruling 2026-08-29 (prod Postgres on the box, cutover drive on). Windows 149..155 had been closed by hand all day; 155 was the last one a person typed and the first this timer closed, 2026-08-29T01:54Z. Unit source: deploy/postmark-world2-clearing.{service,timer}, script deploy/world2-clearing.sh
units.cadence: 05:45 and 17:45 UTC — census Decision 3's own marks, the same two postmark-settlement.timer carries
units.stale_means: The candle stops. Windows pass their close and stay open, claims sit pending in a window that will not clear, and every downstream read — standing tiers, the docket, escrow sufficiency — describes a town frozen at the last close somebody performed by hand. The allowance is one crossing plus an hour, matching the settlement sweep it shares its marks with. NOTE THAT THE STAMP IS WRITTEN ON REFUSAL TOO, deliberately: a clearing that refused (the null-pin guard) has RUN, and this heartbeat answers 'did the lane run', while the service's own non-zero exit is what answers 'did it succeed'. Read both — a fresh stamp with an ALARM-failed beside it means the guard fired, and clearing.json names which one.

units.label: the World 2.0 projection poll
units.activation_owner: Keemin — PARKED at his word 2026-08-31 ~03:45Z ('arm it, disable git ingest'): the World2 shadow mirror is armed on the prod office and is the store's SOLE feeder; the seam closed lawfully (mirror live, one final ingest pass, then this timer disabled). Every sentence in this row was rewritten with the word, per this file's own stripe-watch scar.
units.parked_because: the shadow writer is the store's sole pen (founder-ruled 2026-08-31) — a re-lift from git would launder v1's record into v2's and destroy the writer comparison the shadow era exists to make
units.adopt_command: sudo systemctl enable --now postmark-world2-ingest.timer — ONLY at Keemin's word; re-adopting silently would recommit the ruling this row records
units.cadence: none while parked (the unit file keeps its :04/:19/:34/:49 UTC OnCalendar for the day it is re-adopted)
units.cadence_source: the unit file — disabled with no next fire is this row's healthy state
units.stale_means: not judged while parked. The store's freshness belongs to the SHADOW WRITER now — a mirror failure surfaces in the office journal (loud, fire-and-forget) and the dead-letter queue, never here. When this rail was live its staleness only degraded the doors' advisory reads; the clearing pins its own reads at the candle and refuses on a null law pin regardless.

units.label: the World 2.0 notary
units.activation_owner: Wright — 2026-08-29, PAYING A NAMED DEBT. The notary shipped with 'Nightly TIMER deferred deliberately — the box roll-call manifest law' written into world2/tools/README.md at its merge; the deferral was correct and this row is what settles it. Script deploy/world2-notary.sh, connecting as snapshot_reader and no other role
units.cadence: nightly at 03:20 UTC, jittered up to 2 min — between the 17:45 and 05:45 closes so a certification never races a clearing
units.stale_means: No new certified snapshot binds (acts cursor, window cursor, content sha, law sha, town sha), so the repo stops being able to catch the office rewriting history — gold section 2's whole promise. The allowance is one day plus two hours. TWO THINGS AN OPERATOR MUST KNOW HERE. First, a RED from this unit is usually a FINDING and not a broken timer: an archive is frozen on write, and the pen refuses and names the diff rather than overwriting. Second, as of 2026-08-29 the notary checkout at /srv/world2-lab/notary has NO GIT REMOTE, so its certifications live only on the box they certify; world2-backup.sh carries them off-box as a git bundle as a stopgap, and the push target is teed to Keemin.

units.label: the World 2.0 durability lane
units.activation_owner: Wright — founder ruling 2026-08-29 ('prod Postgres = ON THE BOX with shipped backups, no managed service'). Script deploy/world2-backup.sh. First rehearsed restore from the off-box copy the same night: 6318 rows across 9 tables, every table matching, restore in 1s, projection-equality falsifier GREEN against the restored database
units.cadence: nightly at 04:10 UTC, jittered up to 5 min — after the notary, so the shipped bundle carries that night's certification
units.stale_means: THE STORE STOPS HAVING AN OFF-BOX COPY, and this is the one row in this file where a long silence is not a degraded read but an unbounded loss: every hour past the last successful ship is an hour that dies with the box. The allowance is one day plus two hours. What the lane ships is the pg_dump (RPO no worse than 24h) plus a bundle of the notary checkout, to github.com/wright-starforge/postmark-world2-backups, private, over an SSH deploy key scoped to that one repository. What it does NOT ship is the WAL: measured at about 163 MB/day raw on 2026-08-29, which no git history survives, so the pg_basebackup and the WAL spool are on-box only and cover a bad migration rather than a lost box. That split is deliberate and it is the tee — an object-storage bucket makes the WAL ship a dozen lines. Check the receipt with deploy/world2-restore-rehearse.sh --from-remote, which is the only thing that turns any of this from a hope into a backup.

_custody_readme: §2b — WHO OWNS THE FILES A SERVICE HAS TO WRITE.
Every row above asks whether a mechanism RAN. These ask whether it still can.
On 2026-08-28 a sudo git touched the settlement clone and left root-owned files
inside it. The lane runs as meepo. Root-owned refs, objects and a root-owned
credential store then failed LATER and SEPARATELY — a two-hour pen lockout one
day, a refused 05:45Z crossing the next — with nothing on the box tying either
back to the one act that caused them, because nothing on the box could see the
ownership of a working file at all.
ALARM-custody is its own verdict because its repair is chown, not systemctl. A
row that reported it as ALARM-failed would send the operator to restart a unit
that will fail again the same way in twelve hours.
FIELDS. id · label · path (the root scanned, recursively) · must_be_owned_by
(a username, resolved to a uid on the box — a name that does not resolve is
itself an alarm, never a pass) · why (what breaks when custody slips; required,
same discipline as a unit row's activation_owner) · repair (the command).

custody.label: the settlement clone's git internals
custody.why: This clone is the settlement's whole pen. postmark-settlement.service runs as meepo (its unit says so: 'the clones and push credentials are meepos'), and the sweep writes refs, objects and a commit into it on every crossing, then pushes under a lease. A single root-owned ref or pack from a stray sudo git makes the next write fail — and it fails at whichever step touches that particular file, hours later, looking like an unrelated fault.
custody.repair: sudo chown -R meepo:meepo /srv/postmark-office/settlement-clone && sudo -u meepo git -C /srv/postmark-office/settlement-clone fsck --no-progress

custody.label: the office pen's credential store
custody.why: Every push this box makes reads it — the settlement clone is configured with credential.helper 'store --file /srv/postmark-office/.git-credentials' by settlement-auto.sh itself, and deploy/settlement-escalate.mjs reads the same file to reach the operator queue. A root-owned credential store is the exact shape of the 2026-08-28 two-hour pen lockout: readable by nobody who needs it, and silent until the moment something tries to push.
